act.name: Act 1 — Arrival
act.function: Establish the silence and what it costs to keep it.
act.dramatic_question: Will she let him back in the house?
act.shift: From a closed house to a door left ajar.
act.summary: Marcus returns unannounced; Eleanor absorbs him into the work of the day rather than acknowledge him.

act.name: Act 2 — The Thaw
act.function: Force proximity until speech becomes possible.
act.dramatic_question: Can they be in the same room without the truth?
act.shift: From arm's length to a thaw neither will name.
act.summary: The accident at the crossing puts her in his arms; the locket moves from saddlebag to pocket.

act.name: Act 3 — The Truth
act.function: Say it, survive it, choose each other after.
act.dramatic_question: Is forgiveness possible once it is deserved?
act.shift: From rupture to an embrace at an open door.
act.summary: Marcus confesses. The storm takes the horses and he goes after them; she is afraid for him, which is the answer.

character.name: Eleanor Cade
character.summary: Sixty-one, widowed, running the Cade homestead alone since her daughter drowned. Competence is how she holds grief at arm's length.
character.backstory: Came west at nineteen. Buried a husband at forty-two and a daughter at fifty-four. Has not left the valley since.
character.motivation: To keep the place standing, and to not have to say aloud what she believes about the day Ada died.
character.flaw: Mistakes silence for mercy — to others and to herself.
character.arc_description: From a woman who answers questions with tasks to a woman who says the thing and lets it cost her.
character.internal_goal: To stop blaming her son without having to forgive him.
character.external_goal: Get the homestead through the winter.
character.greatest_fear: That saying it aloud makes it true forever.
character.core_belief: Work is what love looks like when you can't speak.

character.name: Marcus Cade
character.summary: Thirty-four, back after seven years without warning. Carries his sister's locket and the reason he left.
character.backstory: Was at the creek the day Ada drowned and has never told anyone. Left within the month; sent money, never letters.
character.motivation: To be told he is not what he believes he is.
character.flaw: Confesses only when cornered, then calls it honesty.
character.arc_description: From a man performing ease to a man who says the true sentence and survives the silence after it.
character.internal_goal: Absolution he cannot ask for directly.
character.external_goal: Winter over at the homestead and mend what he can.
character.core_belief: A debt can be worked off if you work hard enough.

character.name: Ada Cade
character.summary: Drowned at the creek crossing seven years before the story opens. Present in the film only as objects: a shawl, a locket, a chime by the door.
character.core_belief: Never appears on screen; every design decision about her is an absence decision.

character.name: Reverend Shaw
character.summary: Buried Ada. Believes grief is a thing you can be walked through on a schedule.
character.motivation: To get Eleanor back into the congregation.

creative_decision.name: Decision #14 — score withheld
creative_decision.description: Score withheld across all act-2 kitchen scenes.
creative_decision.rationale: Links sonic_identity.silence_philosophy and Ada's theme (first sounding sc 24).
creative_decision.alternatives_considered: Solo fiddle under sc 12 (rejected: the chime must be the only music Ada gets until the end); low organ pedal (rejected: telegraphs the confession).

creative_decision.name: Ada is never shown
creative_decision.description: No flashbacks, no photographs of Ada's face.
creative_decision.rationale: The locket's portrait is never shown to camera; the audience builds her out of other people's behaviour.
creative_decision.alternatives_considered: A single flashback at the confession — cut: it explains what the silence already carries.

creative_decision.name: One lamp for the confession
creative_decision.description: sc 19 lit by a single practical.
creative_decision.rationale: The scene is about what can be said in the dark.
creative_decision.alternatives_considered: Firelight — rejected as too warm for a rupture.

creative_decision.name: No score until sc 24
creative_decision.description: Music enters only at the final scene.
creative_decision.rationale: Silence is the film's grammar; scoring the grief would do the audience's work for them.
creative_decision.alternatives_considered: A theme under sc 19 — tested and dropped.

creative_decision.name: Scene numbers are not sequential
creative_decision.description: The demo keeps its original scene numbers with gaps.
creative_decision.rationale: The conformance suites address scenes by number; renumbering would break every lookup in both implementations.

scene.purpose: An outside voice names the thing wrongly.

scene.name: EXT. RIDGE FOREST - NIGHT (STORM)

scene.emotional_beat: Fear for him, which is forgiveness starting

scene.name: EXT. FARMHOUSE PORCH - DAWN
scene.summary: The embrace at the open door.
scene.purpose: The door, open, chosen this time.

scene.name: INT. FARMHOUSE KITCHEN - NIGHT (LATER)
scene.summary: Eleanor alone after the confrontation. The lamp is out; the door is still open.

scene.name: EXT. FARMHOUSE YARD - NIGHT (CUT)

sequence.name: The Return
